original_scientific_home: Crall et al. 2020 Biology Letters; original collection and total-count results remain source-owned

secondary_analysis.question: Within Euglossa, is wind associated with male scent-bait-arrival species composition after accounting for site, scent, and linear study day?
secondary_analysis.model: Multinomial conditional species composition; six gated named taxa plus other Euglossa; site + scent + day vs same + within-site centered log(wind)
secondary_analysis.p_value_interpretation: No detected joint composition shift at the chosen site-bait-day-adjusted estimator; not evidence of zero biological wind effect
secondary_analysis.novelty_boundary: Previously published wind-total-arrival association is not a new finding

limitations: Secondary result chosen only after an earlier genus-level support gate failed
70 observation sessions, not 409 independent wind-exposure replicates
Artificial chemical male-bee baits, not flower visitation or pollination effectiveness
Wind not randomized; within-site×bait permutation exchangeability may be violated by time
Sparse taxa, extreme nuisance coefficients and rare meth bait sessions
One forest field system; not cross-region ecological generality
Unverified field-day/time observer and detection corrections
